nodes.description: TFIID, built from TBP and the TBP-associated factors with TAF6 in its core, is required for RNA polymerase II transcription initiation. A destabilized TFIID is proposed to perturb transcription initiation broadly, which is the basis for grouping Alazami-Yuan syndrome with the TAFopathies and with the Cornelia de Lange-like "transcriptomopathies". No study has measured TFIID assembly, promoter occupancy, or the transcriptome in patient material, and why a defect in a ubiquitous general transcription factor yields a tissue-restricted developmental phenotype is unexplained.

evidence.snippet: Alazami‐Yuan syndrome (AYS) is an autosomal recessive Cornelia de Lange‐like syndrome caused by loss of function variants in TAF6.

nodes.description: Biallelic germline TAF6 variants are the initiating lesion. The two founding missense alleles, p.Arg46Cys and p.Ile71Thr, both fall in the N-terminal histone-fold domain through which TAF6 assembles into the TFIID core. Later probands carry a missense allele in trans with a frameshift (c.1052delT, c.1863dup) or a homozygous frameshift (c.610_611delGC). The founding missense alleles retain enough function to support viability: they caused only a slight growth reduction when tested in a yeast taf6 temperature-sensitive strain, which the authors read as compatible with survival of homozygous patients. Whether every allele is hypomorphic, or some combinations are near-null, is not established.
